body.heading: Where in the world is Madagascar?
paragraphs: Madagascar is a country in Eastern Africa, which is part of Africa. It is an island country, surrounded by sea.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Madagascar is Antananarivo.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Madagascar speak Malagasy and French.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Madagascar is the Malagasy ariary.

body.heading: How big is Madagascar?
paragraphs: Madagascar covers about 587,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of South Africa.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: Lemurs are primates native to Madagascar. About nine in every ten of Madagascar's plants and animals live nowhere else on Earth — the island is a world of its own.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Giant baobab trees, some 800 years old, line a dirt road near Morondava like a parade of friendly giants — at sunset they glow orange against the sky.
In this misty rainforest you can hear the indri — the largest lemur — singing its eerie, beautiful song through the trees before you ever see it.
